## Video 289: Samsung HIDES your screen!

- **Video ID:** p7h6iWiKM6M
- **URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p7h6iWiKM6M
- **Published:** Unknown
- **Duration:** Unknown
- **Views:** 17,000
- **Description:** N/A...

### Transcript

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has a wild
new privacy display that can block your
viewing angles from the side on demand.
You can not only toggle it on or off,
but even apply it to only parts of the
screen, like here on this notification.
The oversimplified explanation for how
this actually works is that your display
apparently has some pixels that point
mostly to the front and others that
point mostly to the sides. And Samsung
can selectively turn the sideways
pointing ones off. This means that when
the feature is on, the display gets
dimmer and cuts your resolution in half.
So, you probably won't want to keep it
enabled all the time. Instead, you can
choose to have it automatically turn on
in whatever apps you select. You can
have it turn on for when you enter your
PIN to unlock your phone, or you could
also have it on for pop-up
notifications. Really cool, though. I
thought that the display on the S26
Ultra actually looked a little bit more
grainy than its predecessor, even when
the feature was off. So I think there's
actually a small quality penalty.

## Video 290: Repairable & upgradeable headphones - Fairbuds XL 2025

- **Video ID:** Lmg29gBGQug
- **URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lmg29gBGQug
- **Published:** Unknown
- **Duration:** Unknown
- **Views:** 31,000
- **Description:** N/A...

### Transcript

These headphones can be completely
disassembled in under 5 minutes. They're
fully repairable and they can also be
used to upgrade their predecessor.
They're the brand new Fairbutts XL and
you start by popping off a cover to
access the replaceable battery. Next is
the cover on the other cup which is then
followed by some screws under which
there's a userreplaceable PCB with
access to the buttons and all. Then the
cushions just twist right off leaving
you with the drivers which you can then
remove. And fun fact, these not only
sound better than the predecessor, you
can actually buy these separately, and
you can upgrade your older headphones
with these. Next, you unplug the USBC
toC cable on both ends of the headset.
Then you pull up this fabric to reveal a
latch, which then allows you to pull out
the headband base. And finally, the
whole headband can be pulled apart like
this. And voila, you're done. Just pay
attention to not ruining the little
rubber or silicon seals, which are what
give you the IP54 water resistance.

we took the Apple watch Ultra and the
